documents.title: Vascular surgery consultation
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
Outside vascular surgery group
Date of visit: 01/12/2022

Asked by podiatry to see Mr. Conti for a right plantar forefoot ulcer with a right ABI of 0.62 (left 1.02). He has no rest pain and no calf claudication he can name; the neuropathy may mask some of it. Former smoker. Diabetic on insulin. CAD with prior stent, on aspirin and atorvastatin.
Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: right foot warm, capillary refill sluggish, DP and PT diminished on the right, normal on the left. The ulcer is smaller than podiatry's measurement, clean, no infection.
Impression: peripheral arterial disease of the right leg; neuropathic ulcer that is already healing with offloading.
Plan: no intervention while the ulcer heals. Walking program, continue aspirin and statin, glucose control. Podiatry to keep offloading and wound care. If the ulcer stalls or he develops rest pain, we will see him back for imaging and discussion.

Vascular Surgery

orders.reason: progressive exertional dyspnea and ankle swelling

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Since late summer he gets winded doing things that used to be easy, the stairs, the leaf blower. Ankles swell by evening and are down by morning. Up about 3 kg since June. No chest tightness beyond his usual rare angina. Albuterol doesn't change the breathlessness.
Exam: comfortable at rest. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Both ankles puffy, pitting.
ECG: sinus, unchanged.
A/P: exertional dyspnea and edema in a man with ischemic heart disease; worried about his heart pumping. Cardiology referral sent, they can see him in about 2 weeks; they'll do the workup there. Low salt in the meantime, daily weights. ED for breathlessness at rest or lying flat.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group
Date of visit: 12/02/2022

Known to us for CAD and stable angina. Returns at his PCP's request with three months of steadily worsening breathlessness on exertion and swelling of both ankles. No chest pain, palpitations or fainting.
History: hypertension, type 2 diabetes on insulin, MIs 2014 and 2018, stent 2014, COPD, seizure disorder.
Medications: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin 40, aspirin, metoprolol succinate 50, insulin glargine, valproic acid, albuterol, nitroglycerin PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals: BP 145/90, HR 88, RR 18, SpO2 96% on room air.
Exam: JVD present. S3 gallop. Lungs clear to auscultation. 2+ pitting edema both ankles.
Labs today: Na 138, K 4.5, creatinine 1.2, fasting glucose 160, BNP 900.
Chest X-ray: enlarged cardiac silhouette, no infiltrates.

Impression: new heart failure, presumed reduced ejection fraction on an ischemic basis.
Plan:
1. Furosemide 20 mg each morning. Daily weights; call for a gain of 1 kg in a day or 2 kg in a week.
2. Transthoracic echo next week.
3. BMP in about 2 weeks through his PCP.
4. Continue metoprolol, lisinopril, aspirin, atorvastatin.
5. 2 g sodium diet.

Cardiology

reports.text: Technically adequate study. Left ventricular ejection fraction approximately 30% by visual estimate, reduced systolic function. Right ventricular size and function normal. No significant valvular stenosis or regurgitation. No pericardial effusion. Inferior vena cava normal size.
reports.conclusion: Reduced left ventricular systolic function, LVEF about 30%.

Exam: no JVD seen sitting up. Heart regular, no gallop heard today. Lungs clear. Trace ankle edema.
A/P: HFrEF, EF ~30%, better on furosemide 20. Continue metoprolol, lisinopril. Cardiology follow-up in March. T2DM, A1c today. Low-salt diet reviewed again.

Heart failure with reduced EF (about 30% on echo 12/2022), ischemic. Much improved since starting furosemide; walking more, ankles near normal. Angina rare, nitroglycerin a few times since the winter began.
Meds: furosemide 20, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 20, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, nitroglycerin PRN, metformin, insulin glargine, valproic acid, albuterol.
Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: no JVD, regular, no S3, lungs clear, trace edema.
Impression: HFrEF, compensated. Stable angina.
Plan: continue current medicines. Daily weights. Return 6 months.
